subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Catalytic Converter
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Catalytic Converter.

hook.text: Every modern gas car has a small box in its exhaust that performs chemistry at 800°F.

buildup.text: The catalytic converter uses platinum, palladium, and rhodium to trigger chemical reactions in exhaust gas.

discovery.text: It converts toxic carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides into harmless carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water.

twist.text: Those precious metals make catalytic converters worth hundreds of dollars—thieves steal them in minutes.

climax.text: Since their introduction in 1975, catalytic converters have cut car emissions by over 90%.

punchline.text: A tiny box of rare metals cleans up your exhaust.

quiz.question: What metals are used in a catalytic converter?

details.summary: The catalytic converter uses precious metals like platinum as catalysts to convert toxic exhaust gases including carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, and nitrogen oxides into less harmful substances.
details.whyItMatters: Catalytic converters have eliminated over 99 percent of harmful tailpipe pollutants since their introduction in the 1970s, dramatically improving urban air quality worldwide.
takeaways: Platinum, palladium, and rhodium catalyze chemical reactions
They convert CO, NOx, and hydrocarbons into CO2, N2, and water
Catalytic converter theft is rising due to precious metal values

faq.question: Why are catalytic converters being stolen from parked cars?
faq.answer: They contain platinum, palladium, and rhodium worth hundreds to thousands of dollars. Thieves can remove a converter with a battery-powered saw in under two minutes and sell it to scrap dealers.

faq.question: Do electric cars have catalytic converters?
faq.answer: No. EVs produce zero tailpipe emissions, so they have no exhaust system or catalytic converter. Hybrid vehicles do have them since their combustion engine still produces exhaust gases.
